# messq

See `messq help exit-codes` for the exit-code contract.

## messq

a lightweight, single-binary queue daemon

### Synopsis

messq is a lightweight, single-binary message queue for Linux.

The same binary runs the daemon (serve) and drives it as a client;
every command answers to the same flags, environment variables,
output modes and exit-code contract, so scripts written against one
command keep working against all of them.

```
messq [flags]
```

### Examples

```
  messq version
  messq serve --data-dir /var/lib/messq # noexec: starts a long-running daemon
  messq verify --deep --data-dir /var/lib/messq # noexec: names a machine-specific directory
```

### Options

```
  -a, --addr string         daemon address (unix://, http://, https://) (default "unix:///run/messq/messq.sock")
      --color string        colour: auto|always|never (default "auto")
      --full-ids            print full ULIDs instead of abbreviated ones
  -h, --help                help for messq
  -o, --output string       output mode: auto|table|json|ndjson (default "auto")
  -q, --quiet               suppress narration; data and errors unaffected
      --timeout duration    per-request deadline (0 = none) (default 30s)
      --token-file string   file holding the bearer token, mode 0600
  -v, --verbose count       narrate (-vv dumps each HTTP exchange and the resolved config)
```
